title: Decide what your lab may watch, and why
summary: Before any tool: write down which devices and traffic your home lab may observe, and the one failure you most want to catch.

blocks.title: Write your lab's scope before you plug anything in
blocks.body: A home security lab watches traffic. Before it watches anything, decide what it is allowed to watch and what it is for. That one page of decisions is the boundary every later step builds inside.

columns.name: Lockout/tagout
columns.detail: Before working on a machine, you mark what is safe to touch and what is not. Nobody starts cutting first and checks the tags later.

columns.name: A camera on your own driveway
columns.detail: You can point a camera at your driveway. Pointing it through the neighbor's window is a different thing, even from your own property.

blocks.heading: Consent defines the lab
blocks.body: Owning the router does not make every device on it yours to watch. A roommate's laptop, a guest's phone, or a work computer on your Wi-Fi all carry someone else's communications. In the US, federal wiretap law covers network traffic, and owning a network does not by itself give you authority to capture everything that crosses it. Laws vary by place, and this is not legal advice. The practical rule is simple: the lab watches devices you own or are explicitly allowed to watch, and nothing else. Metadata counts too. A log of who connected where and when says a lot about a person, even without the content.

blocks.heading: Pick the one failure you most want to catch first

items.label: A device of mine starts talking to somewhere new
items.detail: The lab watches connection records: who talked to whom, and when.

items.label: A service on one of my machines is reachable when it shouldn't be
items.detail: The lab starts with a list of what's listening, and re-checks it.

items.label: Something on my network is scanning my other devices
items.detail: The lab watches for one device touching many others, or a decoy nobody should touch.

items.label: Someone outside is trying to log in to something of mine
items.detail: The lab watches the edge: what's exposed, and who knocks.

blocks.heading: A case the table didn't cover
blocks.prompt: Your sensor was meant to see only lab devices, but this morning's log has lines from your roommate's phone. What do you do?
options: Keep the lines; they were captured by accident, so it's fine
Delete those lines and fix the capture so it only sees lab devices
Ask the roommate what the connections were
blocks.explanation: Accidental capture is still capture. Remove what you weren't allowed to collect, then fix the boundary so it doesn't happen again. Asking about the connections would use data you shouldn't have.
